answer: Pulse-window admission uses a rolling horizon of arrival timing: each new identity must submit its first action in a distinct, randomly assigned 200ms slot, and any slot collision voids all colliding registrations. The pulse must show natural jitter, so clones launched in one batch produce a flat traffic shape that fails the variance check. A hollow burst of identical requests is rejected outright. An attacker then pays roughly one second of real-time scheduling delay per identity plus orchestration to stagger traffic, making mass sybil creation slow and costly rather than free.
